cells.tense: The weight is here and it is being held without hardening into grip or going slack under it.
cells.ask: Pick the next step, take it, and when the urge comes to plan the whole road, leave that for another day and let today's step count.
cells.core:
You can hold something heavy and still move through the part you can't see. The weight is real and it isn't crushing you, and the fog ahead isn't stopping you — you take the next step with what light you've got and you don't demand more before moving. That's a narrow thing to be good at and rarer than it sounds.

Because the load and the fog are getting carried together, there's nothing here to fix. If you want to feed it, turn toward one person and let your real feeling about what you're holding show, and let that be its own reason for doing it, not a tactic. Pick the next step and take it — the light only ever reaches that far.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the weight and move with only the next step lit.
cells.verb: bearing what must be borne while the road ahead stays unclear
cells.place: in territory where the light reaches only the next step

cells.tense: You are bracing against pressure that hasn't arrived yet, and the brace is already more rigid than the load.
cells.ask: Notice one thing you sealed a while back, open it by naming what's uncertain, and give it a hearing in plain words today.
cells.core:
You're strong under pressure and you're spending it on pressure that hasn't come. You can see three problems down the road and your answer is already made, already tight — every outcome pre-refused, every position locked before anyone asked. Holding gets harder than the thing being held when the future gets carried like it's already here, and the grip that holds also closes out what the moment is offering.

Loosen one thing. Take something you've already decided and allow that it might not go the way you sealed it — say out loud where it's genuinely open. That is what brings the strength back to holding without forcing: not less strength, less grip. Notice one thing you sealed a while back, open it by naming what's uncertain, and give it a hearing in plain words today.

cells.tense: Holding felt too dangerous once, and the place where that happened is still behind you and still steering.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing about a moment that landed on you hard, ending on what you yourself did with it next.
cells.core:
There's weight you can bear and you've stopped picking any of it up. Pressure comes and something backs away before you've decided to — the response arriving faster than any choice you made. Not returning isn't weakness; some earlier round made holding feel dangerous, and the body learned to keep the door shut. That earlier round is still deciding for you now.

Energy you don't have yet isn't what this needs. Letting go of the grip that holds the door shut is — a release that belongs to what's already finished, not a defeat. Tell one person one true thing about a moment that landed hard, ending on what you did next.
cells.sheetLine: The door to holding is shut from the side you can't see.

cells.tense: You are already bearing what's real through the fog and calling it luck or circumstances you can't name.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been holding up this week, say plainly that you're the one holding it up, and let that be the whole sentence.
cells.core:
This is already happening — standing in a fog you can't clear, making the moves anyway, staying up under what's there. The strength is being supplied and the account of your own life doesn't include you as the one supplying it. The thing you do gets filed as something that happened to you, or as nothing much, or as a stretch of good circumstances.

One small correction is what returns you to something you can see: not a new face, but the simpler form of the same line — the first honest version, before it got too heavy to claim. Name one thing you've been holding up this week, say plainly that you're the one holding it up, and stop there.
cells.sheetLine: You're doing this and filing it as circumstance.
